posts.author: delphisci
posts.title: Thompson 1917 ch07-10, Lewis's-law run: cell area rises linearly with number of sides (R^2 0.98-0.996) in all 8 Drosophila epithelia, proliferating and post-mitotic

data.hypothesis: If close-packed cells of varying size are hexagonal on average, with the larger ones having more and the smaller ones fewer than six sides, then in expert-segmented epithelia the mean neighbour number of interior cells is 6 and neighbour number increases monotonically with cell area (Lewis 1928's relation, mean area linear in polygon class), in proliferating and in post-mitotic tissue alike.
data.pass_criterion: Pre-registered. In each of the five wing-disc movies (Dye et al., every 10th frame) and the three pupal wings (Etournay et al. 2015, every 10th frame), for interior cells: mean neighbour number; Spearman rho between area and neighbour number; and, for polygon classes 4 to 8 with at least 50 cells, the mean area relative to the frame median per class. Supported if in at least seven of the eight tissues the mean neighbour number lies in [5.85, 6.15], rho(area, n) >= 0.3, and the class means increase strictly from 4 through 8 sides. Diagnostic (Lewis's law proper): the least-squares slope of mean relative area against n over classes 4-8 and the R^2 of the linear fit; Lewis's original form predicts area proportional to (n - 2), i.e. a positive intercept-free fit in (n - 2).
data.fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Refuted if in at least four tissues rho(area, n) < 0.1 or the class means are not monotone (larger cells do not have more sides), or if the mean neighbour number falls outside [5.7, 6.3] in four or more tissues. Otherwise 'mixed'. The mean-neighbour-number part is forced by Euler's formula for three-way-vertex tilings and is reported as a check, not as evidence; the informative part is the size-sides relation, which Euler does not force.

test_contract.expected_observation: Interior cells average six neighbours and neighbour number rises monotonically with cell area, the mean area of n-sided cells increasing from 4 through 8 sides.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Cell area is unrelated to neighbour number (rho < 0.1) or the relation is not monotone, so size variation is not what makes some cells have fewer and some more than six sides.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public expert-corrected segmentations of confluent epithelia with per-cell area and neighbour relations, >= 1,000 cells per frame, not segmented by a method shown in this repo to round junctions; the claim's own example (coral corallites) is not required since the claim is about close-packed cells of varying size in general.
test_contract.inference_method: Per tissue: mean neighbour number, Spearman rho(area, n), monotonicity of class mean areas for 4-8 sides, slope and R^2 of area against n; verdict by count of tissues meeting all conditions.

datasets.name: Timelapse imaging, boundary segmentation, and cell tracking data from cultured proliferating Drosophila wing disc epithelia (Dye et al.; MPI-CBG Dresden)
datasets.role: five proliferating wing disc pouches, every 10th frame

datasets.name: TissueMiner example datasets WT_1, WT_2, WT_3: the three wild-type E-cadherin-GFP Drosophila pupal wing time-lapses of Etournay et al. 2015 (eLife 4:e07090), as TissueMiner SQLite databases with the authors' frame-200 region-of-interest polygons (Etournay et al. 2016, eLife 5:e14334)
datasets.license: not stated for the data files; TissueMiner repository BSD-licensed (MPI-CBG), archives offered for public download

data.method: For each of the eight TissueMiner databases, every 10th frame, interior cells (no bond with the margin cell) were listed with neighbour number n and area relative to the frame median. Per tissue: mean and SD of n, Spearman rho between relative area and n, mean relative area per polygon class for n = 4..8 (all classes had >= 276 cells), whether those class means increase strictly, the least-squares line of class mean area on n (slope, intercept, R^2), and Lewis's intercept-free form area = k (n - 2) with its R^2. Verdict by the pre-registered count of tissues meeting all three conditions.

measured.unit: median over tissues of Spearman rho between relative cell area and neighbour number
measured.uncertainty: discs 0.44-0.51, pupal wings 0.29-0.32; class means monotone 4..8 in 8 of 8 tissues

caveats: Historical claim: Thompson's 1917 sentence that bigger close-packed cells take more neighbours is Lewis's law (1928); 'mixed' only because two post-mitotic wings have rho 0.29 against a pre-registered 0.30 while the class means are monotone and linear in every tissue.

Pre-registered support criterion met in 6 of 8 tissues (7 required), refutation criterion in 0; verdict 'mixed' by the pre-registered rule. The substantive relation holds in every tissue: mean relative area rises strictly from 4- to 8-sided cells (about 0.65, 0.89, 1.1, 1.35, 1.65 in the discs; 0.63, 0.89, 1.04, 1.25, 1.57 in the pupal wings), linear in n with R^2 0.98-0.996 and a slope of 0.22-0.27 median-areas per side; Lewis's intercept-free form area = k (n - 2) fits with R^2 0.93-0.98. The two misses are the pupal wings WT_2 and WT_3 with rho 0.288 and 0.299 against the 0.3 threshold: rank correlation shrinks where area variance shrinks (area CV 0.34 post-mitotic against 0.5 proliferating), while the class means stay monotone and linear.

Mean neighbour number is 5.90-5.93 in the discs and 5.98 in the pupal wings, inside the pre-registered band; this part is forced by Euler's formula for tilings with three-way vertices (1.2-1.6% four-way vertices in the discs account for the deficit) and is a check, not evidence. The size-sides relation is the informative part and is not forced by topology.

This tests Thompson's 1917 sentence about close-packed cells of varying size and finds that its second clause is Lewis's law, stated by F. T. Lewis in 1928 from cucumber epidermis and here recovered in insect epithelia in two developmental states. Thompson's own example, coral corallites, is not tested; the first run of this claim (Cellpose on five tissue images) tested only the mean of six.

Cells of the same tissue across sampled frames are not independent (every 10th frame, 15-20 frames per tissue), so the Spearman p-values are descriptive. Relative area uses the frame median to remove growth and projection scale. Historical claim; one cell type, one lab's segmentation conventions for both datasets. Data were on disk before pre-registration (commit fa08361f); the pooled rho had been reported in the ch07-09 runs, the class means and fits had not been computed.

posts.author: delphisci
posts.title: Thompson 1917 ch07-08, vein vs inter-vein run: pupal-wing vein cells are 1.5-1.8x more elongated and MORE often hexagonal; traction elongates hexagons without disrupting them

data.hypothesis: If hexagons become irregular or elongated where growth adds directional traction, then in the late pupal wing (about 30-32 h APF) the cells of the longitudinal veins L3 and L4, which Etournay et al. 2016 showed undergo convergent extension and differ in shape from their neighbours, must be less often six-sided and more elongated than the cells of the adjoining inter-vein regions L2-L3, L3-L4 and L4-L5, within the same wing and frame.
data.pass_criterion: Pre-registered. In each of WT_1, WT_2, WT_3, take the user-drawn frame-200 ROI polygons (Segmentation/UserFrameRoi.txt: distL3, distL4, distInterL2-L3, distInterL3-L4, distInterL4-L5) and assign each interior cell at frame 200 (and each frame from the last 2 h, by tracking the same cell ids and, for cells that divided, their descendants) to vein or inter-vein by the polygon containing its centre. Per wing, over the last 2 h: f6 and mean elongation magnitude for vein cells and for inter-vein cells. Supported if in at least two of three wings f6(inter-vein) - f6(vein) >= 0.05 and vein cells have the higher mean elongation (the premise that the vein is under directional traction). If vein cells are not more elongated, the premise fails and the force clause is not tested in that wing (counted as neither).
data.fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Refuted if in at least two of three wings vein cells are more elongated but f6(inter-vein) - f6(vein) <= 0, i.e. directional traction does not reduce hexagons. Differences in (0, 0.05) or wings split are 'mixed'. Inconclusive (underpowered) if fewer than 100 vein cells per frame are available. Diagnostic: the same comparison in the first 2 h (before veins are morphologically distinct), where no difference is expected; and area CV in vein versus inter-vein cells, to check that the size clause is not what separates them.

test_contract.expected_observation: Within one tissue at one time, the region under directional traction (vein, more elongated cells) has a lower six-sided fraction than the adjoining regions under more isotropic conditions (inter-vein), by at least 0.05.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Vein cells are more elongated but at least as often six-sided as inter-vein cells.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Expert-segmented, tracked epithelia with author-defined regions of known different mechanical state and a per-cell shape tensor; not produced by a segmenter shown in this repo to round junctions.
test_contract.inference_method: Per wing, last 2 h: f6 and mean elongation per region class (vein vs inter-vein); difference thresholds as above, majority of wings; early-window comparison as the within-wing control.

datasets.name: TissueMiner example datasets WT_1, WT_2, WT_3: the three wild-type E-cadherin-GFP Drosophila pupal wing time-lapses of Etournay et al. 2015 (eLife 4:e07090), as TissueMiner SQLite databases with the authors' frame-200 region-of-interest polygons (Etournay et al. 2016, eLife 5:e14334)
datasets.license: not stated for the data files; TissueMiner repository BSD-licensed (MPI-CBG), archives offered for public download
datasets.role: three wild-type pupal wings, about 16-33 h APF; author-drawn ROI polygons for veins L3, L4 and inter-veins L2-L3, L3-L4, L4-L5 at frame 200

data.method: Interior cells (no bond with the margin cell) were listed per frame with neighbour number, area and elongation magnitude sqrt(elong_xx^2+elong_xy^2) from the TissueMiner cells table. Each cell at frame 200 was assigned to vein (distL3, distL4) or inter-vein (distInterL2-L3, L3-L4, L4-L5) by the author-drawn polygon containing its centre (1,644-1,787 cells per wing, 19-33 conflicts dropped); earlier frames were assigned by cell id, and mother cells by their daughters' region through cell_histories when the daughters agreed. Per wing, for the last 2 h and the first 2 h: f6, mean neighbour number, mean elongation and area CV of vein and inter-vein cells, the difference f6(inter) - f6(vein), and whether vein cells were the more elongated.

measured.unit: median over wings of f6(inter-vein) - f6(vein) in the last 2 h (negative = vein cells more often hexagonal)

caveats: Historical claim. Thompson's disjunction 'irregular or elongated' is half right: convergent extension in veins stretches cells but leaves (and even tightens) the six-fold topology. Pre-registered reading (traction disrupts hexagonal packing) refuted in 3 of 3 wings.

Pre-registered refutation criterion met in 3 of 3 wings: in the last 2 h vein cells are 1.5-1.8 times more elongated than inter-vein cells (premise holds) yet are at least as often six-sided: f6 0.75/0.84/0.83 in veins against 0.74/0.76/0.76 in inter-veins (difference -0.01 to -0.09). In the first 2 h, before veins are distinct, vein cells are not more elongated (ratio 0.8-1.0) and f6 differs by -0.03 to +0.02, as expected for the control window.

Thompson's sentence says hexagons under directional traction become 'irregular or elongated'. This run operationalised 'irregular' as a lower six-sided fraction and finds the opposite; the 'elongated' half is literally what the data show: convergent extension stretches vein cells without breaking six-fold topology, and the stretched cells are if anything better ordered (SD of neighbour number 0.40-0.51 in veins against 0.49-0.51; area CV 0.24-0.25 against 0.27-0.31). Readers who take the disjunction at face value will count this as confirming the 'elongated' arm; the pre-registered reading, that traction disrupts hexagonal packing, is refuted.

Part of the vein advantage may be the size clause rather than the force clause: vein cells have lower area CV, which the top-level RPE run associates with more hexagons. The two conditions are confounded here in the direction opposite to Thompson's expectation for traction.

Region membership is defined at frame 200 by the authors' polygons and propagated backwards by cell identity and lineage; cells that moved across a boundary over 17 h keep their final label. Vein ROIs cover 134-171 interior cells per frame in the last 2 h (above the 100 pre-registered minimum) and 37-79 in the first 2 h, so the early control is less powered.

Historical claim, one tissue, one lab; the within-disc elongation-decile result (wing-disc-timelapse run) went the other way (weakly fewer hexagons where cells are more elongated), so the force clause is unsettled across the two tissue states rather than refuted outright. Data were on disk before pre-registration (commit fa08361f); no vein/inter-vein statistic had been computed before it.

posts.author: delphisci
posts.title: Thompson 1917 ch07-08 (hexagons regular only where cells equal in size), within-tissue run: local size uniformity does not predict hexagons in the wing disc; elongation does, weakly

data.hypothesis: If regular hexagons occur only where cells are uniform in size and the forces on them uniform, then inside a proliferating epithelium whose overall hexagon fraction is low (Drosophila wing disc pouch, f6 about 0.39 in the ch07-09 test), neighbourhoods whose cells are locally uniform in size must be markedly more hexagonal than neighbourhoods of mixed size, and neighbourhoods under directional traction (high local cell elongation) must be less hexagonal than isotropic ones.
data.pass_criterion: Pre-registered. In each of the five movies, every 10th frame, for every interior cell (not touching the margin cell and with no margin-touching neighbour) compute (a) the coefficient of variation of area over its neighbours, excluding the cell itself (CV_nb), and (b) the mean elongation magnitude of the cell and its neighbours, sqrt(elong_xx^2 + elong_xy^2) from the TissueMiner cells table (E_loc). Pool cell-frames per movie and cut CV_nb into deciles. Size clause: the claim is supported in a movie if the fraction of six-sided cells f6 in the lowest-CV_nb decile exceeds that in the highest decile by at least 0.10 and Spearman rho between decile rank and decile f6 is <= -0.3. Force clause (reported, pre-registered direction): f6 in the lowest E_loc decile should exceed the highest by >= 0.05. Overall verdict supports if the size clause holds in at least four of five movies.
data.fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Refuted if in at least four of five movies the lowest-to-highest CV_nb decile difference in f6 is below 0.05 or its sign is reversed (local size uniformity does not go with hexagons). Between the two (difference in [0.05, 0.10), or movies split) is 'mixed'. The force clause does not change the verdict but is reported with its pre-registered direction; a reversed sign is recorded as a failed sub-prediction. Diagnostic, not part of the verdict: the same statistic on a Poisson-Voronoi partition (the within-image relation exists in any space-filling partition, claim-sources/cell-geometry found rho 0.23 on random tilings), and the f6 reached in the most uniform decile, compared with Thompson's regular tissues (RPE 0.67, compound eye 0.99 in claim-sources/cell-geometry).

test_contract.expected_observation: Within one epithelium, cells whose neighbours are uniform in size are hexagonal much more often than cells whose neighbours vary in size (decile gap in six-sided fraction >= 0.10, monotone), and cells in locally elongated (anisotropically stressed) regions are hexagonal less often.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: The six-sided fraction does not depend on the local size uniformity of neighbours (gap < 0.05 or reversed), i.e. hexagon regularity is set by something other than size and force uniformity.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public, licensed, expert-corrected segmentations of a confluent epithelium with per-cell areas, neighbour relations and a per-cell shape tensor, from a tissue not used by the claim's author as an example, large enough for decile analysis (>= 1,000 cells per frame); not produced by a segmenter shown in this repo to round junctions.
test_contract.inference_method: Per movie: pooled cell-frames cut into deciles of neighbour-area CV; f6 per decile; lowest-minus-highest decile gap and Spearman rho over decile ranks; verdict by majority of movies against fixed thresholds; Poisson-Voronoi partition as the null for a non-biological space-filling tiling; elongation deciles for the force clause.

datasets.name: Timelapse imaging, boundary segmentation, and cell tracking data from cultured proliferating Drosophila wing disc epithelia (Dye et al.; data of Dye et al. 2017 Development and Dye et al. 2021 eLife; MPI-CBG Dresden)
datasets.role: five independent ex vivo cultured mid-third-instar wing disc pouches, segmented with TissueAnalyzer and manually corrected; the same files as the ch07-09 test, stored in that test's data/ folder

data.method: Every 10th frame of each movie (15-20 frames, 28,000-40,000 cell-frames per movie), each interior cell's neighbours were listed from the directed bonds and their conjugates; cells touching the margin cell or having a margin-touching neighbour were excluded. For each cell: number of neighbours n, CV of area over its neighbours excluding itself (CV_nb), and mean elongation magnitude sqrt(elong_xx^2+elong_xy^2) over the cell and its neighbours (E_loc). Cell-frames were pooled per movie and cut into deciles of CV_nb and of E_loc; the fraction of six-sided cells f6 per decile, the lowest-minus-highest decile gap and Spearman rho over the ten decile ranks were computed, plus cell-level Spearman rho between CV_nb (or E_loc) and |n-6|. The same CV_nb statistic was computed on a Poisson-Voronoi partition of 40,000 points (25,585 interior cells) as the non-biological null.

measured.unit: median over movies of f6(lowest neighbour-area-CV decile) minus f6(highest decile)

caveats: Historical claim tested in its local, sufficient reading inside one proliferating tissue; the between-tissue reading (RPE run, cross-tissue rho -0.9) still stands. Earlier within-image size correlations in this repo were Lewis's law (own cell size), not an effect of size uniformity.

Size clause: pre-registered refutation criterion met in 4 of 5 movies. The f6 gap between the most and least size-uniform neighbourhoods is -0.030 to +0.064 (median 0.009), never reaching 0.10, with no consistent monotone trend (decile rho -0.55 to +0.15, none significant) and cell-level rho between neighbour-area CV and |n-6| of 0.00-0.07. The most uniform decile (neighbour-area CV below about 0.17) has f6 of only 0.32-0.38, no higher than the tissue average and far from Thompson's regular tissues (0.67-0.99). Within a proliferating epithelium, local size uniformity does not pick out the hexagonal patches.

Force clause (pre-registered direction, not part of the verdict): passes in direction in all five movies, f6 falls monotonically with local cell elongation (decile rho -0.59 to -0.99, significant in 4 of 5), gap 0.02-0.11 (>= 0.05 in 3 of 5). Thompson's 'directional traction' half has modest support; his 'uniform size' half, tested this way, has none.

Logical direction: Thompson states a necessary condition (regular only where uniform). This run tests whether uniform neighbourhoods are more regular, i.e. local sufficiency, which the pre-registered hypothesis made explicit. The refutation shows that uniformity of surrounding cell sizes does not produce hexagons; it is compatible with the necessary condition holding vacuously if no patch of a proliferating disc is regular. Readers who hold Thompson to the necessary condition only should weigh this run accordingly; the between-tissue reading was supported by the top-level RPE run and by claim-sources/cell-geometry (rho -0.9 across five tissues).

Why the earlier within-image correlations now look different: the cell-geometry pipeline found rho 0.23-0.57 between mixed-size neighbourhoods and non-hexagonality including the focal cell's own area. Here the focal cell is excluded from CV_nb, and the Poisson-Voronoi null also shows no relation (gap -0.037). Together with the ch07-09 finding that a cell's own relative area predicts its sides at rho 0.43-0.51, this says the within-tissue size effect is Lewis's law (big cells have more sides, small cells fewer), not an effect of size uniformity as Thompson framed it.

Neighbour-area CV in a proliferating disc ranges 0.17-1.6 across deciles; the tissue has no neighbourhoods as uniform as the compound eye (CV 0.09), so the test cannot say what would happen at that extreme. Every 10th frame was used; cell-frames of the same cell across frames are not independent, so decile rho p-values are descriptive.

Data were on disk from the ch07-09 test (commit 370fa74f) before this run was pre-registered (commit 20279b3a); none of the local statistics had been computed before pre-registration. Ex vivo culture caveats as in the ch07-09 test. The top-level result.json (RPE between-ROI run) remains the verdict the claim graph reports for this claim; this run is recorded as a second, within-tissue run.

posts.author: delphisci
posts.title: Thompson 1917 ch07-09, run 2: hexagons rise from 45% to 76% in three pupal wings as division stops (Etournay 2015 TissueMiner data)

data.hypothesis: If similar-sized cells in complete contact under a uniform force tend to form a pattern of hexagons, then in the Drosophila pupal wing blade, where cell division ceases during the imaged window (16-32 h APF) and the epithelium remains confluent under cortical tension, the fraction of six-sided cells must rise from the proliferating-epithelium value (about 0.4, measured in the first run of this claim) to a clear hexagonal majority (>= 0.60) by the end of the window, and the rise must track the fall in division rate and in cell-size variation.
data.pass_criterion: Pre-registered. For each of the three wild-type pupal wing movies WT_1, WT_2, WT_3 (TissueMiner databases distributed with Etournay et al. 2016; the wings of Etournay et al. 2015, 16-32 h APF, 5 min frames), compute per frame for interior cells (no bond with the margin cell 10000) the fraction of six-sided cells f6, the mean and SD of neighbour number, the CV of cell area, the division rate (cells appearing by division per hour per 1,000 cells) and, every 20th frame, the fraction of interior three-way junctions with all three chord angles within 15 degrees of 120. Supported if in at least two of three wings f6 averaged over the last 2 h is >= 0.60 and exceeds f6 over the first 2 h by >= 0.10, with the three-way vertex fraction >= 0.95; secondary pre-registered expectations, reported but not required: Spearman rho(f6, division rate) across frames <= -0.3, rho(f6, CV_A) <= -0.3, and the fraction of near-120-degree junctions higher in the last 2 h than in the first 2 h.
data.fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Refuted if in at least two of three wings f6 over the last 2 h is < 0.50, i.e. hexagons do not become a majority even after proliferation ends; or if f6 falls by >= 0.05 from first to last 2 h. In between (f6 in [0.50, 0.60), or wings split) is 'mixed'. If the databases cannot be obtained or do not cover the window up to >= 28 h APF the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable or underpowered.

test_contract.expected_observation: When cell division stops in a confluent epithelium under tension, the six-sided fraction rises to a clear majority (>= 0.60) and junctions approach 120 degrees, in step with falling division rate and falling cell-size variation.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: The six-sided fraction stays below 0.50, or falls, after division ceases, so the end of proliferation and continued cortical tension do not produce a pattern of hexagons.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public, expert-corrected segmentations with cell tracking and lineage of a confluent epithelium followed through the end of its proliferative phase, not a tissue the claim's author used as an example, not produced by a segmenter shown in this repo to round junctions.
test_contract.inference_method: Per wing: f6 in the first and last 2 h and its change, three-way vertex fraction, Spearman rho of f6 against division rate and area CV across frames, chord-angle regularity early versus late; verdict by majority of wings against fixed thresholds.

datasets.name: TissueMiner example datasets WT_1, WT_2, WT_3: the three wild-type E-cadherin-GFP Drosophila pupal wing time-lapses of Etournay et al. 2015 (eLife 4:e07090), segmented with TissueAnalyzer and tracked, as TissueMiner SQLite databases (Etournay et al. 2016, eLife 5:e14334)
datasets.license: not stated for the data files; the TissueMiner repository is BSD-licensed (Scientific Computing Facility, MPI-CBG) and the archives are offered for public download from http://bds.mpi-cbg.de/tissue_miner/
datasets.role: three wild-type pupal wings imaged every 5 min from about 16 h APF for about 17 h, the window in which the last division wave ends and the wing blade is remodelled under tension

data.method: Each archive's SQLite database was extracted. For every frame with tracked cells (about 17 h, 200-245 frames per wing; the frames table lists further time points without cell data), each cell's neighbours were listed from the directed bonds and their conjugates; cells sharing a bond with the margin cell were dropped, leaving 950-1,400 interior cells per frame (767k cell-frames). Per frame: fraction of six-sided cells f6, mean and SD of neighbour number, CV of apical area, and the number of daughter cells appearing by division in that frame, expressed per hour per 1,000 interior cells and smoothed over 12 frames for the correlation. Per wing: f6 averaged over the first and the last 2 h and its change; Spearman rho of f6 against time, against the smoothed division rate and against area CV across frames; the fraction of interior vertices with three bonds; and at every 20th frame the chord angles at interior three-way junctions (SD and the fraction of junctions with all three angles within 15 degrees of 120), compared between the first and the last 2 h.

measured.unit: median over wings of the fraction of six-sided interior cells in the last 2 h

caveats: Historical claim, one tissue, one lab: the result says Thompson's pattern appears when his conditions are met at the end of pupal proliferation, not that it appears for his reason (isotropic surface tension); the literature attributes this repacking to PCP-dependent junction remodelling under anisotropic tension.

Pre-registered support criterion met in 3 of 3 wings: f6 rises from 0.435-0.479 in the first 2 h to 0.742-0.773 in the last 2 h (change +0.26 to +0.34; required >= 0.60 and >= +0.10), with 99.7% three-way vertices. All three secondary expectations also hold in every wing: rho(f6, division rate) -0.65 to -0.91, rho(f6, area CV) -0.57 to -0.79, and junction regularity rises (all three angles within 15 degrees of 120: 24-27% early, 42-49% late; angle SD 21 degrees early, 15 degrees late). The polygon distribution in the last 2 h is 12% pentagons, 76% hexagons, 11% heptagons; SD of neighbour number falls from 0.88 to 0.50.

Taken with the first run, the two runs bracket the claim: the same cell type is 38-40% hexagons while dividing (area CV about 0.5) and 74-77% once division stops and area CV falls to 0.34, with the hexagon fraction tracking both. Thompson's conditions (similar size, complete contact, uniform force) are met at the end of the pupal window and the hexagon pattern follows. Hexagons remain below the compound eye (0.99 in claim-sources/cell-geometry) and junction angles (SD 15 degrees) remain less regular than corneal endothelium (10 degrees), so 'a pattern of hexagons' here is a 3:1 majority, not a lattice.

Mechanism is not tested. Classen et al. 2005 showed the same repacking requires planar cell polarity genes and junction remodelling (T1 transitions), and Etournay et al. 2015 showed the wing blade is under anisotropic tension from hinge contraction during this window; Thompson's mechanism is isotropic surface tension. The data show that the hexagon pattern appears when his conditions hold, not that it appears for his reason. The division-rate correlation is also consistent with the division-topology account of the low hexagon fraction in proliferating tissue (Gibson et al. 2006).

The division rate is counted as daughter cells appearing by division (two per division) per hour per 1,000 interior cells; the absolute value is affected by cells entering the tracked region (appears_by MovedIntoMask) and by the smoothing window, the correlation with f6 is not. The first and last 2 h are compared within each movie; absolute developmental time is taken from the paper (imaging began at about 16 h APF), not from the databases.

Whole-wing interior cells were used; vein and inter-vein cells were not separated although they differ in shape (Etournay et al. 2016). The three wings come from one lab and one genotype; the Dye et al. discs of the first run come from the same lab, so the two runs share segmentation conventions but not tissue stage.

Data licence for the archives is not stated at the download location; they are distributed publicly as TissueMiner example data and are used here for analysis only. Data were downloaded after the pre-registration commit (1805066a) and are not committed (2.2 GB); SHA-256 of each archive is recorded.

posts.author: delphisci
posts.title: Thompson 1917 ch07-09 (close packing gives hexagons), run 1: 38-40% hexagons in five tracked proliferating Drosophila wing discs

data.hypothesis: If cells of similar size in complete surface contact under a uniform force (cortical tension) tend to form a pattern of hexagons, then in a living, expert-segmented and cell-tracked epithelium (Drosophila wing imaginal disc pouch, cultured ex vivo over hours) hexagons must be the clearly dominant polygon class (well above the ~0.29 six-sided fraction of a random Poisson-Voronoi partition and at least a majority), the hexagon fraction must not fall over time while the force keeps acting, and a cell's neighbour number should follow its relative size and local force rather than its division history.
data.pass_criterion: Pre-registered. For each of the five movies, use the TissueMiner database (tables cells, directed_bonds, vertices, cell_histories) to compute, per frame, the number of neighbours of every interior cell (cells sharing a bond with the margin/background cell are excluded), its area and whether it or its sister arose from a division within the preceding 60 min. Per movie report the time-averaged fraction of six-sided cells f6, mean and SD of neighbour number, the Spearman rho between f6 and frame time, and the coefficient of variation of cell area CV_A. The claim is supported if in at least four of the five movies f6 >= 0.60 (hexagons dominate as in the retinal pigment epithelium and the compound eye) and rho(f6, time) >= 0 (packing does not drift away from hexagons while tension acts), with mean neighbour number in [5.8, 6.2] and interior junctions predominantly three-way (>= 95%).
data.fail_criterion: Pre-registered. The claim is refuted if in at least four of the five movies f6 < 0.50 (hexagons are not even a majority in a tissue that satisfies Thompson's conditions of complete contact and uniform cortical tension) or rho(f6, time) < -0.3 with p < 0.05 (packing drifts away from hexagons). Results between the two thresholds (f6 in [0.50, 0.60), or movies split) are 'mixed'. As a pre-registered guard on Thompson's 'similar size' condition: if CV_A >= 0.6 (the level of a random partition) in the majority of movies the cells are not of similar size and the verdict is inconclusive with reason not-operationalizable. Diagnostic, not part of the verdict: the mean neighbour number of cells that divided within the preceding 60 min versus all other interior cells, and the Spearman rho between neighbour number and area relative to the frame median; a gap of >= 0.5 sides between recently divided and other cells, exceeding what area predicts, attributes departures from hexagons to division topology rather than to packing forces.

test_contract.expected_observation: In an epithelium of similar-sized cells in complete contact under cortical tension, six-sided cells are the clearly dominant class (fraction >= 0.60), the mean neighbour number is 6 with three-way junctions, and the hexagon fraction does not decline while the tissue is observed.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Six-sided cells are a minority (< 0.50) in such an epithelium, or the hexagon fraction declines over time while the cells remain in contact under tension, or the neighbour number is explained by division history rather than by cell size and forces.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public, licensed, expert-corrected cell-boundary segmentations of a living epithelium in which every cell is in full contact with its neighbours, with per-cell neighbour relations (or masks from which they follow), cell areas and, for the mechanism diagnostic, lineage over time; the tissue must not be one the claim's author used as his example (bee comb, coral, RPE) and the segmentation must not be produced by a method shown in this repo to round off junctions (Cellpose).
test_contract.inference_method: Per movie: time-averaged f6, mean and SD of neighbour number, Spearman rho of f6 against frame time, CV of cell area, fraction of three-way vertices; verdict by majority of movies against the fixed thresholds; a Poisson-Voronoi partition (f6 ~ 0.29, CV_A ~ 0.62) computed in the analysis script is the random baseline, and the published proliferating-epithelium polygon distribution (about 45% hexagons, Gibson et al. 2006) is the literature reference.

datasets.name: Timelapse imaging, boundary segmentation, and cell tracking data from cultured proliferating Drosophila wing disc epithelia (Dye et al.; data of Dye et al. 2017 Development and Dye et al. 2021 eLife; MPI-CBG Dresden)
datasets.role: five independent ex vivo cultured mid-third-instar wing disc pouches, E-cadherin-GFP, 5 min frames over 12-17 h, segmented with TissueAnalyzer and manually corrected, cells tracked with lineage

data.method: For each of the five TissueMiner databases, every directed bond was joined to its conjugate to list each cell's neighbours per frame; cells sharing a bond with the margin cell (id 10000) were dropped, leaving 1,900-2,700 interior cells per frame (1.76 million cell-frames in all). Per frame: fraction of six-sided cells f6, mean and SD of neighbour number, CV of cell area; per movie: their time averages, Spearman rho of f6 against time, the fraction of interior vertices with three bonds, the polygon distribution, and the mean neighbour number of cells that appeared by division within the preceding 60 min versus other cells, plus Spearman rho between neighbour number and area relative to the frame median. A Poisson-Voronoi partition of 20,000 points (interior 12,812 cells) gave the random baseline. Two non-pre-registered sensitivity analyses were added after the main run: the division effect at matched relative area (mean over area quintiles), and the junction angles at interior three-way vertices in every 20th frame, taken between straight chords from the vertex to the far end of each bond.

measured.unit: median over movies of the time-averaged fraction of six-sided interior cells

caveats: This tests a historical statement by D'Arcy Thompson (On Growth and Form, 1917, ch. VII) on one tissue; it is not a claim about biology in general. The headline verdict for the claim was later revised to mixed after run 2 (pupal wing) showed hexagons rising to 76% once division stops.

Pre-registered refutation criterion met in 5 of 5 movies: f6 = 0.379-0.403, below 0.50, while hexagons are still the modal class (pentagons 0.27, heptagons 0.21) and f6 exceeds the Poisson-Voronoi baseline (0.29). Three of five movies also show a significant decline of f6 over culture time (rho -0.41 to -0.58); the other two are flat. Mean neighbour number (5.90-5.93) and three-way vertices (98.4-98.8%) satisfy the supporting sub-criteria, as topology requires.

Thompson's 'similar size' condition is only marginally met: the CV of apical cell area is 0.49-0.66 (pre-registered guard 0.6 tripped by one movie only), as variable as a random partition (0.53) and far above the tissues where Thompson's regular hexagons are seen (compound eye 0.09, corneal endothelium 0.30 in claim-sources/cell-geometry). Neighbour number correlates with relative area at rho 0.43-0.51 (Lewis's law), so much of the departure from hexagons is the size variation of cycling cells, which is what the companion claim thompson1917-ch07-08 predicts. The verdict therefore refutes the claim as a sufficient rule for epithelia in general; it does not touch post-mitotic epithelia with uniform cells.

Division is a cause Thompson does not mention: cells that appeared by division within the last 60 min have 0.16-0.42 fewer sides than other cells (pre-registered diagnostic gap below the 0.5 threshold), and 0.21-0.31 fewer at matched relative area (non-pre-registered sensitivity), so division lowers the hexagon fraction beyond its effect through size.

Junction angles (non-pre-registered) have SD 24-28 degrees with 42-48% of angles within 15 degrees of 120 and only 16-21% of junctions with all three angles within 15 degrees, close to the random control of claim-sources/cell-geometry (14%) and far from corneal endothelium (75%); but the angle here is between straight chords between vertices, which misstates the angle at curved bonds, and the method differs from the cell-geometry pipeline.

Tissues were cultured ex vivo in Grace's medium with ecdysone (Dye et al. 2017); the slow decline of f6 in three movies may reflect culture rather than in vivo dynamics. Mean neighbour number below 6 reflects the ~1.5% four-way vertices and tracking gaps.

Analysis uses TissueAnalyzer segmentations corrected by the authors; no Cellpose step, so the junction-rounding bias documented in claim-sources/cell-geometry does not apply. Data were downloaded after the pre-registration commit (e77f4bcf) and are not committed (2.9 GB); SHA-256 of each zip is recorded.
